pair_verdict.headline: SPLIT VERDICT: NO's care flip is MANUFACTURED BY BUDGET (a deliberate, durable rebuild-era reset that doubled a stable pre-storm ratio); Houston's care posture is ABSORBED-BY-GROWTH (the diaspora landed in a static care lane — flat-to-cut dollars FY05-FY06 — and the care ratio never re-based: it drifted 0.27 pre-shock -> 0.16-0.20 by FY26 as the cage lane grew faster than care).
pair_verdict.no_side: 0.164 (FY04 actual) -> 0.095 trough (FY06) -> 0.311 (FY11) -> 0.313-0.318 (FY17-19) -> 0.365 (FY22) [Certain-as-published]. The post-storm ratio PLATEAUES at ~2x pre-storm and never re-enters the old band — a structural reset (Library Fund, NORD/Parkway mills, Health dept rebuild), exactly the public-budget flip class.
pair_verdict.houston_side: 0.270 (FY04 budget-col) -> 0.243 (FY05) -> 0.228 (FY06, care CUT 1% in dollars while Police +5%) -> 0.245 (FY07, first care wave +15.7%: Health +62%, Parks +40%) -> 0.187 (FY22) -> 0.248 (FY24, subtotal-read) / ~0.21 (component-read) -> 0.199 (FY26) -> 0.160 (FY27). NO care-ratio break, no flip: care/resident rose 64->92 (+44%) FY04->FY26 but cage/resident rose 245->461 (+88%) — cage ran away WITH the population, care roughly tracked it. The newcomers landed in STATIC care capacity; Houston's response was growth-absorptive, not care-progressive.
pair_verdict.the_twin_law: Same shock, opposite budget postures: the city that LOST people re-based its care ratio UP through its own ledger (deliberate budget choice); the city that GAINED people never re-based (care lanes static; the ratio fell). Population shock alone does NOT produce a care flip — the NO flip required the rebuild-millage/ledger mechanism.

cage_resident_arc.HO: 245.3 (FY04) -> 294.0 (FY07) -> 461.1 (FY26): cage-per-resident +88% — the CRIME+ input: Houston absorbed the diaspora into a cage lane that grew twice as fast as care

diaspora_composition_notes.who_arrived: Texas took ~250,000 evacuees (Wikipedia New Orleans diaspora <- FEMA/state counts, Sep 2005); Houston city alone sheltered '>150,000 people from New Orleans' (Wikipedia Houston <- Houston Chronicle 'Katrina's Human Legacy' Aug 27 2006) [Certain-as-published]. Permanent-stay class tracked upstream at 200,000-300,000 never-returned (SPINOFF_IDEAS banked-studies lane) [Likely].
diaspora_composition_notes.age_family_income: Wikipedia diaspora article: ~40% of 1.5M Gulf evacuees could not return home; 25% relocated <10mi; 25% >450mi [Certain-as-cited]. Income/family-structure granularity (age bands, single-parent %, income deciles) NOT yet machine-ingested here — flagged as the open composition lane; the Harris County evacuee-profile studies (Kaiser/Katrina-era surveys) are the named next source.
diaspora_composition_notes.who_left_NO: NO lost >50% pop (>230k); Black residents, renters, elderly, and low-income disproportionately (Wikipedia New Orleans <- Nelson/Ehrenfeucht/Laska Cityscape 2007 + Morse 2008) [Certain-as-cited]; July 2006 census est 223,000; 2007 273,000.
diaspora_composition_notes.care_ratio_response: NO: care ratio RE-BASED (0.16 -> 0.31-0.37 plateau) — budget-led. HO: care ratio never re-based (0.27 -> 0.16-0.20) — care lanes static while cage grew with the population. The arrival-class composition (Black, renter, low-income, disproportionately younger families) matches the cage-lane growth pressure: Police +$600M (FY05->FY27) absorbed the demand side.

budget_per_resident.HO: 451 (FY04) -> 463 (FY06) -> 746 (FY22) -> 845 (FY26): +87% over 22 years — steady growth-city economics, no shock signature

population_shock_response_comparison.response_read: NO's per-resident care spend quadrupled (60->292) because the city CHOSE a rebuild that re-based care; Houston's per-resident care grew only +44% (66->92) while the city absorbed the largest single-city Katrina intake — capacity-per-head barely moved: absorption, not expansion.

confidence.NO_series: HIGH — banked Certain-as-published (official adopted-book tables, page-cited, flip falsifier already tested upstream)
confidence.Houston_series: MEDIUM-HIGH — (a) FY05/06/07 + FY22/24 read via VISION from scanned image PDFs (no text layer) but every subtotal arithmetic-checked (4/6 books reconcile to ≤0.4%; FY2005 3,597/2,990/1,510-dollar sub-read deltas = prior-year restatements; FY2024 book has a REAL printed-subtotal discrepancy of ~181M between component lines and the printed PS subtotal, carried openly with both cage reads); (b) FY2004 Houston row is BUDGET-column-based (Actual column restatement-affected, both readings in the row); (c) FY26 dept-grain is delta-0-Certain; (d) interpolations 2001-2009 population are linear between decennial anchors and labeled
confidence.pair_conclusion: MEDIUM-HIGH: the direction (NO flips and plateaus, Houston drifts 0.27->0.16-0.20) survives the basis-change check (both series carried on fire-excluded, courts-included convention; NO's flip already survived its own GF-only falsifier upstream)

falsifier.claim: Houston absorbed the Katrina diaspora WITHOUT a care-ratio flip (static care capacity; absorption not budget-manufactured expansion), while NO's flip was budget-manufactured
falsified_if: A Houston care flip exists OUTSIDE the General Fund: the all-funds/capital lanes (Metro 2012 parks bonds, 2023 parks bond, library capital, Houston Parks Board MOU) could carry a care expansion invisible to GF ratios — TEST: recompute Houston care/cage at all-funds grain (the II_GFS Table-I all-fund volumes exist for every era read here); if all-funds care/cage jumps >1.5x off its pre-2005 band after 2005 and never re-enters, the 'absorbed by growth' verdict fails.

The 0.27->0.16 Houston drift is a Fire-inflation artifact: Fire grew 281M->732M (2.6x) and is excluded from cage. If Fire is INCLUDED in cage (NO-series convention keeps fire_flagged OUT of cage but a fire-inclusive control read exists), Houston's ratio still falls 0.165->0.123 (FY04->FY26) and never flips — the drift is genuinely cage-side (Police +$624M).

NO's flip is a population-denominator artifact: NO falsifier already tested this upstream (GF-only + all-funds checks) — survives; the twin-city control HERE is the strongest confirmation: if the flip were mechanical (any big population shock flips care/cage), Houston should have flipped TOO — it did not.

The FY24 Houston subtotal discrepancy hides a care break: the printed-vs-component 181M gap is on the PUBLIC SAFETY side; recomputing with the component-sum cage (1,042.7M) gives ratio 0.207 — still inside the 0.16-0.21 no-flip band.
